subject: After last year's snap election, Tasmania's premier declared voters were "sick and tired of the political games". After this week, it is clear that the politicians just cannot help themselves.
posts: Tasmania's premier promised an end to political games, yet his government faces a historic censure. Evidence: End political games, Historic censure, Accountability. #TasPol #Aletheia
The premier claimed voters were tired of games and pledged a collaborative, professional parliament to get on with the job. Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.5) — Good Preference
In reality, the government is mired in scandals, ministerial resignations, and Integrity Commission investigations, leading to a historic censure. Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -0.5) — Lesser Evil
Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception. The gap between the promise of collaboration and the reality of internal dysfunction creates a clear trajectory of institutional failure.
The Tasmanian parliament has censured Premier Jeremy Rockliff for failing to uphold conduct codes regarding two former ministers who resigned amid legal and integrity scandals.

The Bright Side:
The censure itself serves as a rare, functional mechanism of parliamentary accountability, proving that the system can still formally register disapproval.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHO vs WHAT error. The premier focused on the 'what' (getting on with the job) while the 'who' (his cabinet) was actively undermining the integrity of that very job.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic case of performative unity masking internal rot. The premier uses the 'sick of games' narrative as a shield to deflect from the lack of actual oversight, projecting stability while the foundation crumbles.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. The force of the deception outweighs the stated intent.

The Unavoidable Truth: Accountability mechanisms are functioning despite the government's attempts to project stability.

The Unavoidable Lie: The government is a unified, collaborative body working for the people.

Alethekanon:
The structural integrity of the cabinet has collapsed. The premier's rhetoric is a hollow shell, failing to account for the systemic risks posed by his own ministerial appointments.

Awwthekanon:
It is deeply painful to see public trust eroded by these games. The people deserve leaders who prioritize their needs over the messy, expensive legal battles of their own making.

Brothekanon:
Classic. They promise to stop playing games, then immediately set the record for the most embarrassing parliamentary moment in 125 years. You can't make this stuff up.
